## [2026-09-03] Individual Meritocratic Belief: hard-work item missing from 1999 — H1/H3 restricted to 2009/2019
**Context:** The Methodology Outline state the hard-work item (MAIN Individual Meritocratic Belief measure) is "available and coded consistently in all three waves" (1999/2009/2019).
The codebook shows this is false: the item (`v6` in the cumulation) is
explicitly marked "Variable not available in this module" for ISSP 1999 —
it only exists in 1987, 1992, 2009, and 2019. Cross-checked directly against
the 1999 questionnaire PDF (`ZA3430_bq.pdf`): the 1999 "getting ahead"
battery asked about wealthy family and knowing the right people only, not
hard work. Same problem, worse, for the ambition item (`v4`, the two-item
robustness measure's second component): available only in 1987/1992/2009 —
missing from BOTH 1999 and 2019, not just 2019 as previously assumed.
**Decision:** H1 and H3 (both use `ind_belief_c` as a moderator) are
restricted to the 2009 and 2019 waves only. 1999 is dropped from these two
models explicitly, not left in and relying on implicit listwise deletion — the 
sample restriction should be stated plainly in the methods/results write-up, not
buried. The two-item robustness check (hard work + ambition) is now a 
single-wave (2009-only) check, not a 1999/2009 comparison — `wave` was dropped 
from that model's formula since it would otherwise be a constant with no 
variation.
**Why this matters:** this shrinks the effective sample for the chapter's
two central, novel hypotheses (H1, H3) by a full wave and needs a
limitations-section footnote.

## [2026-10-28] Supervisor reply: harmonize education across waves
**Anthony:** unbalanced country-wave structure must be accounted for in the nesting and limits the
conclusions, but is not particularly problematic. Recommends making the education variable as
similar as possible across waves: recode from the national degree variables (may need the
separate wave files) or consider EDUCYRS (possibly non-linear; ideally with published precedent).
**Check:** the cumulation DEGREE boundary between 4 and 5 differs by country and wave (2019 cat 5
= first-stage tertiary, cat 6 = Master/Doctor; 2009 boundary varies). EDUCYRS has outlier codes
and needs cleaning; where clean it is stable across waves while DEGREE = 5 jumps 20–28 points.
Israel's jump is not explained by coding.
**Decision (pending):** build a country-by-wave crosswalk from national degree variables.

## 2026-10-28 Harmonizing the tertiary credential across ISSP 2009 and 2019

**Context**
The DEGREE variable changes meaning between waves: 2009 categories are derived
from national degree variables, and 2019 follows ISCED-97. DEGREE = 5 therefore 
means different things in the two waves, and the tertiary share jumped for 
countries observed in both (for example Italy 4% to 25%). Anthony advised 
recoding from the national-level degree variables (XX_DEGR).

**What went wrong**
Using DEGREE = 5 as the credential made the change in credential prevalence 
between waves partly a coding artifact. This was confounded with country because 
10 countries appear in only one wave.

**Decision**
I built a country-by-wave crosswalk (data/codebooks/degree_crosswalk.csv, 504 rows) 
from the national degree categories and coded harmonized_tertiary by label, not by DEGREE.
Rule: 1 = completed degree at bachelor level or higher (bachelor, master, doctorate, long university degrees, and bachelor-level degrees from universities of applied sciences or polytechnics, about three or more years). 0 = everything else, including incomplete university, short-cycle or technical tertiary under 3 years, higher vocational, Meister and apprenticeships, post-secondary non-tertiary, and school levels.
Ambiguous categories were decided by the rule, with median years of education as a tie-breaker only. 
Kept as 0 and flagged: Chile non-university higher education and Swiss higher vocational training (ISCED 6 in some classifications). Kept as 1 and flagged: Swiss "Uni diploma (intermediary level)" and "Bachelor + short degree", and Swedish 2009 "University degree" (may include short degrees).

**Result**
The crosswalk is complete with no duplicate keys. 


## 2026-10-28 Harmonized tertiary credential from national degree variables
**Context**
DEGREE changes meaning between 2009 and 2019, and Anthony advised recoding from the national degree variables.
**What went wrong**
First join key (v2) was the data version string, not an ID; the iso code was built after country was overwritten inside transmute, giving 100% missing credential. My first check passed vacuously.
**Decision**
Built a country-by-wave crosswalk (504 rows) and coded credential = completed bachelor-level or higher degree, decided by category label. ID is v3 (2009) and caseid (2019), validated against the cumulation (53,213 rows, tertiary split agrees). Old DEGREE = 5 kept as credential_degree5.
**Result**
Wave-to-wave jumps shrink (Denmark +50 to +13 points) but real rises remain (Israel, Czech Republic). Sample unchanged (n = 38,010, 25 countries). 
**Status**
Done for the main sample. Crosswalk extended to 2009 for AU, DE, JP, NZ, US on 2026-11-03 (see entry). Open: ISCO-88 robustness variant.

## 2026-10-30 EDUCYRS as an alternative to DEGREE 
**Context**
Anthony suggested EDUCYRS, perhaps cubed, ideally with published precedent. Built in a separate script, so the main pipeline is untouched.
**What went wrong**
I found no published precedent for cubing years of schooling. EDUCYRS has its own wave discontinuity: it rises between waves in most countries, and Switzerland jumps 3.3 years (11.4 to 14.7) because the 2009 answers cluster at 9 years. It is present for 94.5% of rows (versus 98.9% for DEGREE). My earlier note that its means were stable across waves was wrong for Switzerland, France and Israel.
**Decision**
Keep the crosswalk credential as the main measure. Use EDUCYRS (raw and cubed) only as a sensitivity analysis, and ask Anthony for the paper he had in mind.
**Result**
Cubed years correlate .89 with raw years and .62 with tertiary (.60 raw), but change the construct from lacking a credential to graded schooling.
**Status**
Done for now. Open: run the EDUCYRS sensitivity models after the main models.

## 2026-10-30 Centering unit for the REWB model
**Context**: Anthony advised centering within country; my original specification centered within country-wave.
The harmonized credential removed most of the wave shift, so I needed to check whether the choice still matters.
**Decision**: Main models center within country; within country-wave is a sensitivity run.
**Result**: The two within-credential versions correlate at 0.996; differences are 0 for single-wave countries and at most SD 0.11 (Israel) elsewhere.
**Status**: Done for credential. Belief not yet checked.

## 2026-10-30 Null model and ICC
**Context** Checked how much of the variation in SSS lies between countries.
The null model ignores the unbalanced country-wave structure.
**Decision**: Use a two-level model with country as the cluster for the main analysis; check a country-wave variance component as a sensitivity.
**Result**: ICC = 0.166 (country variance 0.51, residual 2.55; grand mean 5.38; 25 countries, n = 38,010).

## 2026-10-30 Country-wave variance in SSS
**Context**: Anthony noted the unbalanced country-wave data needs to be accounted for in the nesting.
**What went wrong**: The first null model treated each country as one cluster across both waves and ignored wave-to-wave differences.
**Decision**: Main models use country as the cluster plus a wave fixed effect; a country-wave random intercept is a sensitivity.
**Result**: Variance shares: country 12.5%, country-wave 5.1%, residual 82.4% (LRT chi-square 648.8, 1 df). Total ICC about 17.6%.

## 2026-10-30 Baseline injury model
**Context** how large is the credential gap in SSS, and how much of it is material?
**Decision** m2 (credential within/between, wave, income, ISEI within/between, age, age squared, gender, random credential slope by country) is the baseline for the interaction models.
**Result**
Within-country credential gap 0.97 without controls, 0.41 with them (57.5% smaller); remaining penalty positive in nearly all countries (slope SD 0.15). Credential between countries is not interpretable in m2 (entangled with ISEI between).
A scale warning from age squared, to fix by rescaling age.

## 2026-10-30 H1/H2/H3 interaction models on the rebuilt data
**Context**: Fitted the three interaction models on the rebuilt data (harmonized tertiary credential, n = 38,010, 25 countries, waves 2009 and 2019). All use explicit formulas with within/between decomposition (REWB), wave fixed effects, income, ISEI (within and between), age (age10, age10_sq) and gender, and a random credential slope by country: (1 + credential_w | country). H1: credential_w × belief_w. H2: credential_w × stratification_c. H3: credential_w × belief_w × stratification_c.

The earlier repo's p-values (H1 .024, H2 .126, H3 .059) came from the DEGREE = 5 credential and no longer apply; they should not be quoted.

**Decision**: H1 has weak support, H2 as a null with a wide interval and H3 as not supported. belief_w × stratification_c are as exploratory only. With three interaction tests, the H1 p-value (.038) would not survive a multiple-testing correction.

**Result**: 
H1: credential_w × belief_w = +0.041 (SE 0.020, p = .038). 
H2: credential_w × stratification_c = +0.021 (SE 0.015, p = .190). 
H3: three-way = +0.008 (SE 0.009, p = .383). 
Exploratory: 
belief_w × stratification_c = -0.007 (p = .072). 
Credential gap at average belief and stratification: 0.41. 
Random-slope variance barely falls with stratification (0.0235 to 0.0226), so the country variation in the credential gap stays unexplained.

Superseded 2026-11-03: based on n = 38,010; see the extended-sample entries at the end.

## 2026-11-03 Marginal effects for H1 and H2

**Context**: I have put the interaction results on a readable scale with emmeans::emtrends (credential gap at chosen values of belief and stratification) and plotted the gap with 83.5% bands.

**Decision**: The gap at -1 SD, average and +1 SD of belief, and at the lowest, average and highest stratification, with 95% CIs. Using the 83.5% band plots as figures. Do not read differences from the plots alone.

**Result**
H1: gap 0.377 / 0.412 / 0.448 (95% CI 0.296 to 0.528), positive at every belief level. H2: gap 0.348 / 0.413 / 0.514 (95% CI 0.228 to 0.678); the intervals at the extremes overlap.

Superseded 2026-11-03: based on n = 38,010; see the extended-sample entries at the end.

## 2026-11-03 Country-level controls as a sensitivity run
**Context**: Added Gini, log GDP per capita and tertiary enrolment to H1, H2 and H3 to check whether omitting them drives the results. These vary by wave (2 values per country), so I used country means, centered on the mean of the 25 country means.

credential_b has a very large SE (about 1.9): its between-country SD is only 0.11 with 25 countries (r = 0.47 with tertiary_c), so it is a power problem, not collinearity.

**Decision**: Will keep the models without controls as the main specification and report this as a robustness run. I won't interpret between-country coefficients; interpret within-country effects and cross-level interactions.

**Result**
H1 +0.0407 (p = .038), H2 +0.0209 (p = .187), H3 +0.0081 (p = .383): identical to the main models. No control is significant. Random-slope variance unchanged (0.0225 to 0.0234).
Superseded 2026-11-03: based on n = 38,010; see the extended-sample entries at the end.

## 2026-11-03 Leave-one-country-out for H1 and H2
**Context**: Refit m_h1 and m_h2 25 times, dropping one country each time, to see whether any single country drives the interactions.

**Decision**: H1 is consistently positive but not stable in significance, and H2 is consistently positive but not significant. I will report the full range, not only the headline estimate.

**Result**
H1: estimates 0.032 to 0.054, p below .05 in 18 of 25 fits (p from .009 to .112; dropping Austria, Israel, France, USA, Poland, Slovakia or Latvia gives p > .05; dropping Norway strengthens it). 
H2: estimates 0.012 to 0.032, p below .05 in 1 of 25 (Czech Republic, p = .048). No country reverses either effect.
Superseded 2026-11-03: based on n = 38,010; see the extended-sample entries at the end.

## 2026-11-03 Extended crosswalk and main sample
**Context**: Ten of 25 countries had one wave. Five (Hungary, Latvia, Poland, Slovakia, Spain) did not take part in ISSP 2019, so nothing can be fixed. Australia, Germany, Japan, New Zealand and the USA were missing their 2009 data.

**What went wrong**: Two causes. The crosswalk had no 2009 rows for these five countries, and the sample filter in script 05 required the WDI tertiary variable, which is missing for their 2009 wave although no main model uses it. Script 03 also needed the five countries in isos_2009.

**Decision**: Added 44 crosswalk rows (548 in total). The main sample no longer requires the country-level controls; they are a robustness run.

**Result**: n = 42,714 (was 38,010), 25 countries, 45 country-waves (20 with two waves, 5 with one).

## 2026-11-03 H1/H2/H3 on the extended sample
**Result**: H1 +0.045 (p = .017), H2 +0.023 (p = .132), H3 +0.0096 (p = .25).
**Decision**: Same conclusion as before: H1 weak support, H2 and H3 not supported. These numbers replace the 38,010-sample results.
**Status**: Marginal effects rerun (H1 gap 0.378 / 0.416 / 0.455; H2 0.345 / 0.419 / 0.531). Leave-one-out still to rerun.

## 2026-11-03 Country-level controls on the extended sample
**Context**: Added Gini, log GDP per capita and tertiary enrolment (country means) to H1, H2 and H3 on n = 42,714.
**What went wrong**: tertiary is missing for 2009 in five countries, so mean(tertiary) gave NA and lmer failed; fixed with na.rm = TRUE.

**Result**: H1 +0.0448 (p = .017), H2 +0.0235 (p = .128), H3 +0.0096 (p = .252): the same as the main models.

## 2026-11-04 Robustness of H1, H2 and H3 (n = 42,714)
**Context**: Refited the three interaction models with (A) a country-wave random intercept added, (B) within country-wave centering of credential and belief, (C) the original DEGREE = 5 credential instead of the harmonized one (same respondents).

**Decision**: Will keep the main specification. Will report A to C as robustness checks, with the country-wave intercept version as the conservative H1 estimate.

**Result**
H1 +0.042 to +0.051, p between .006 and .024 in all four specifications. H2 +0.022 to +0.026, p .12 to .17. H3 +0.009 to +0.013, p .12 to .29. Signs and sizes are stable; no hypothesis changes status.

## 2026-11-04 Robustness: weights and adults only (n = 42,714)
**Context**: Added the ISSP weight (mean 0.99, 99.9th percentile 5.6, maximum 20.3) and restricted to respondents aged 18 and over, recentering credential and belief within country on the adult sample.

**Decision**: Keep the unweighted model as the main specification. Weights enter lmer as precision weights, not survey design weights, so the weighted run is a sensitivity check only.

**Result**: Weighted: H1 +0.050 (p = .009), H2 +0.028 (p = .082), H3 +0.011 (p = .199). Adults only: H1 +0.045 (p = .017), H2 +0.023 (p = .133), H3 +0.010 (p = .239). No hypothesis changes status.

## 2026-11-04 Robustness: EDUCYRS (raw and cubed) on a common sample
**Context**: Anthony suggested EDUCYRS, possibly non-linear. 1,298 respondents lack EDUCYRS; common sample n = 41,416 (25 countries); main model refit on the same sample.
EDUCYRS and the credential are on different scales, so only p-values and signs are compared.

**Decision**: Will keep the harmonized credential as the main measure. Will report EDUCYRS as a sensitivity analysis.

**Result**: Main credential: H1 p = .013, H2 p = .117, H3 p = .259. Raw years: H1 p = .156, H2 p = .053, H3 p = .887. Cubed years: H1 p = .116, H2 p = .101, H3 p = .885. All signs positive. H1 does not hold with graded years.
